claim: Real property valuation protests must be signed and filed with the county board of equalization after the assessor completes the assessment roll and on or before June 30.
The county board of equalization meets to decide protests beginning on or after June 1 and ending on or before July 25; counties over 100,000 population may extend the hearing deadline to August 10.
A county board of equalization action may be appealed to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission (TERC) on or before August 24, or September 10 if the county extended its protest hearing deadline.
To perfect a TERC appeal, the notice of appeal must be filed within 30 days of the board of equalization's final order.

Protests of omitted-property assessments or clerical-error corrections are filed with the county board within 30 days after mailing of the notice; the board's action may be appealed to TERC within 30 days of its final decision.
Real property is valued at its actual value; agricultural and horticultural land is valued at 75% of actual value.
An owner wanting a homestead exemption must file an application with the county assessor of the county where the homestead is located after February 1 and on or before June 30 of each year.
Failure to file the application timely is a waiver of the exemption for that year.
Where applicable, qualified claimants' homesteads are exempt for a percentage of the exempt amount limited by section 77-3506.03, with the percentage determined by household income.
Form 458 (Homestead Exemption Application) is filed with the county assessor; an Application for Transfer must be filed by August 15 if moving to a new homestead.
cite: Nebraska Homestead Exemption Application Form 458 | Dept. of Revenue

Documentary stamp tax is imposed on the grantor executing the deed upon transfer of a beneficial interest in or legal title to real estate.
Rate is $3.32 per $1,000 of value or fraction thereof for transfers before January 1, 2032, and $2.32 per $1,000 for transfers on or after January 1, 2032.
Exempt deeds include those to/from the U.S., State of Nebraska or political subdivisions, deeds securing or releasing a debt, and corrective deeds.
Deeds between spouses, between ex-spouses conveying property acquired or held during the marriage, or between parent and child without actual consideration are exempt.
The register of deeds must be presented a signed statement certifying the exemption, with supporting evidence maintained by the signer and available to the Department of Revenue.
A trust deed may be sold by the trustee under an express power of sale (nonjudicial), or at the beneficiary's option foreclosed as a mortgage on real property.

Before the trustee exercises the power of sale, a notice of default must be recorded with the register of deeds; notice of sale may be given after not less than one month (two months if farm property under the statute).
Notice of sale is published once a week for five consecutive weeks, the last publication at least 10 and not more than 30 days before the sale.
At least 20 days before the sale, the trustee must mail notice of the time and place of sale by registered or certified mail to persons who recorded a request for notice.
The trustor or subordinate lienholders may cure the default by paying the amount due within one month (two months in farm cases) of recording the notice of default.
In judicial foreclosure, the owner may redeem any time before the court confirms the sale by paying the decree amount, interest and costs.
Land taken in execution may not be sold until notice is published once a week for four successive weeks in a county newspaper and posted at the courthouse door and five other public places.
Sales made without the required notice are set aside on motion by the court.
Mortgagor's interest is terminated when the sheriff or master commissioner accepts the highest bid, subject to the redemption right and court confirmation.
A district court judge may confirm a sale after the officer's return, on motion and ten days' notice to the adverse party (if made in vacation).
Thirty days after death, a successor may collect personal property by affidavit if the estate's personal property, less liens, does not exceed $100,000.

Thirty days after death, a successor may file an affidavit with the register of deeds claiming the decedent's real property if the decedent's real property interest does not exceed $100,000 (valued from the assessment rolls less taxes due).
A personal representative has the same power over title to estate property as an absolute owner, exercisable without notice, hearing or court order unless the court orders otherwise.
Transfer on death deeds, a non-probate transfer, must be recorded before the transferor's death (see transfer-on-death-deed).
Nebraska imposes an inheritance tax (not an estate tax) on interests transferred at death, including jointly held property except the part contributed by the other owner.
Close relatives: 1% of the clear market value received in excess of $100,000 for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2023.
Uncles, aunts, nieces, nephews and their lineal descendants: 11% over $40,000 for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2023.
All other persons: 15% over $25,000 for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2023.
Bequests in trust to an in-state association for exclusively charitable purposes in this state are exempt from inheritance tax.

Recorded instruments need a blank 3 x 8.5 inch space at the top of the first page, size 8.5x11 to 8.5x14, and each party's name typed or printed beneath the signature.

Property taxes are due December 31 following the levy; from that date taxes on real property are a first lien until paid or extinguished.

The owner, occupant or lienholder may redeem a property sold for taxes; the right expires when the purchaser files an application for tax deed with the county treasurer.
Redemption requires paying the certificate amount with statutory interest plus subsequent taxes, issuance fee and administrative fee.
Purchaser may apply for a tax deed within nine months after three years from the sale (two years for vacant and abandoned real estate).
If rent is unpaid, the tenant fails to pay within seven calendar days after written notice of nonpayment, the landlord may terminate the rental agreement.
For material noncompliance, written notice may state termination not less than 30 days after receipt if the breach is not remedied within 14 days.
District and county courts have jurisdiction over forcible entry and detainer complaints.
Forcible detainer lies against tenants holding over, including tenants failing to pay rent when due, and against judgment debtors in possession after execution sales.
Writ of execution must be executed by the officer within ten days of receipt, restoring possession to the plaintiff.
Forcible detainer lies against a judgment debtor in possession after an execution sale and against holdover tenants.
